# mdk — machin desktop kit

> Native desktop apps in machin (MFL): GPUI-style GPU UI in one draw call per frame, hot reload that keeps state.

Each page of the docs has its own llms.txt; fetch only what the task needs.
Repository: https://github.com/javimosch/machin-desktop · agent skill: https://github.com/javimosch/machin-desktop/blob/master/SKILL.md · machine-readable API: `./mdk guide` (JSON).

## Pages

- [Getting started](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/guide/llms.txt): Install, first app, state, dev loop, release builds, project layout.
- [Layout & styling](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/layout/llms.txt): Elements, modifiers, the flexbox rules, wrapping text, virtual lists, scrolling.
- [Hot reload that keeps state](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/hot-reload/llms.txt): How dev reload works, what survives it, the arena rule, the error overlay, its limits.
- [Benchmarks: mdk vs MyGo](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/benchmarks/llms.txt): MyGo's own scenes, same machine, both on the GPU — numbers, method, caveats, how to reproduce.
- [API reference](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/api/llms.txt): Every framework function: containers, content, widgets, layout, style, state, input, format.
- [Internals](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/internals/llms.txt): Host ABI, element records, the one-call renderer, text shaping cache, memory model.
- [Notes — the dogfood app](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/notes/llms.txt): A micro-SaaS-style markdown notes dashboard built with mdk: nickname, stats, editor + live preview, autosave to .md files.
- [Building mdk apps with an agent](https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/agents/llms.txt): llms.txt, SKILL.md and `mdk guide`: everything a coding agent needs to build an mdk app first try.

## What mdk is

mdk (machin desktop kit) builds native desktop apps in machin (MFL). The UI is a
function of state run every frame (`func view()`), laid out by a small flexbox
written in MFL, and drawn on the GPU in one instanced draw call per frame by a
C host (SDL3 + OpenGL 3.3, HarfBuzz text). In development the app is a shared
object the host reloads on every save: the window stays open and state kept in
the host store (`state_int`/`set_int`, ...) survives.

## Minimal app

```
func view() {
    n := state_int("count", 0)
    col()
    fill()
    center()
    gap(16.0)
        text(str(n), 56.0)
        bold()
        row()
        gap(10.0)
            if button("Increment") { set_int("count", n + 1) }
            if button_ghost("Reset") { set_int("count", 0) }
        end()
    end()
}
```

## Commands

- `./mdk new <appdir>` — scaffold an app directory with app.src (a counter)
- `./mdk dev <appdir>` — build the app as a .so, open the window, rebuild on every save; the window and state survive; build errors draw over the last good frame
- `./mdk build <appdir> [-o out]` — one release binary with the app linked in (no reload, sleeps when idle)
- `./mdk shot <appdir> out.ppm [--size W H] [--frames N] [--click X Y] [--type TEXT] [--key NAME] [--wheel DY]...` — render N frames after a script of real SDL input events (in order: clicks, text input, keys like Return / Backspace / ctrl+a / shift+Home, wheel), then save a screenshot; convert out.ppm out.png to view
- `./mdk check <appdir>` — typecheck the app with the framework (machin encode), no window
- `./mdk guide` — print this JSON

## Headline numbers (MyGo's own benchmark scenes, same Linux laptop, both on GPU)

- CPU per frame: list 0.48 vs 2.83 ms, grid 3.9 vs 37.6 ms, document 0.52 vs 35.9 ms
- grid/document: mdk holds 60 fps, MyGo ~19-21 fps
- release binary 2.6 MB vs 10.1 MB; memory at rest 76.5 vs 116 MB
- one machine (i5-11320H, Mesa, X11); MyGo's own Apple M5 numbers are much faster than here
